options: These are dead tissues and form wood
They provide flexibility to plant due to their thickened walls
These are present in the bark of a tree only
Growth occurs in plants due to division of cells of these tissues
questions.solution: Meristematic tissues, or simply meristems, are tissues in which the cells remain forever young and divide actively throughout the life of the plant. Cells within the meristematic tissues are self-renewing, so that each time they divide, one cell remains identical to the parent while the other can specialize and become part of another plant structure. The meristematic tissue is therefore self-sustaining.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements about classification of plants is correct?
options: Thallophytes have well differentiated body design
Vascular system is not found among Bryophytes
questions.solution:
Mosses and liverworts are lumped together as bryophytes, plants lacking true vascular tissues, and sharing a number of other primitive traits. They also lack true stems, roots, or leaves, though they have cells that perform these general functions.
Bryophytes do not have a true vascular system and are unable to pull water and nutrients up from the ground at any significant distance. Lacking this specialised system distinguishes bryophytes from ferns and flowering plants. It is for this reason that they are considered to be rather primitive plants.

questions.q:
Paragraph: Three sides of a trapezium are each equal to 6 cm . Let $\alpha \in\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ be the angle between a pair of adjacent sides.
Question: If the area of the trapezium is the maximum possible, then what is $\alpha$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Length of three sides of trapezium $=6 \mathrm{~cm}$ Let $A E$ be height of trapezium.
$\begin{aligned} & \text { In } \triangle \mathrm{ADE}, \mathrm{AD}^2=\mathrm{AE}^2+\mathrm{DE}^2 \\ & \Rightarrow 6^2=\mathrm{AE}^2+\mathrm{x}^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{AE}^2=36-\mathrm{x}^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{AE}=\sqrt{36-\mathrm{x}^2} \end{aligned}$ Area of trapezium $=\frac{1}{2} h(a+b)\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{36-x^2}(6+6+2 x) \\ & A=(6+x) \sqrt{36-x^2} \end{aligned}$ Given, Area of trapezium is maximum. $\begin{aligned} & \frac{d A}{d x}=\frac{d}{d x}\left[(6+x) \cdot \sqrt{36-x^2}\right] \\ & =(6+x) \cdot\left(\frac{-2 x}{2 \sqrt{36-x^2}}\right)+\sqrt{36-x^2} \end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\sqrt{36-x^2}-\frac{x(6+x)}{\sqrt{36-x^2}} \\ & =\frac{36-\mathrm{x}^2-6 \mathrm{x}-\mathrm{x}^2}{\sqrt{36-\mathrm{x}^2}}=\frac{36-6 \mathrm{x}-2 \mathrm{x}^2}{\sqrt{36-2 \mathrm{x}^2}} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{dA}}{\mathrm{dx}}=0 \Rightarrow 36-6 \mathrm{x}-2 \mathrm{x}^2=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{x}^2+6 \mathrm{x}-36=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}^2+3 \mathrm{x}-18=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}^2+6 \mathrm{x}-3 \mathrm{x}-18=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}(\mathrm{x}+6)-3(\mathrm{x}+6)=0 \\ & (x+6)(x-3)=0 \end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad x=-6$ or 3 . Since $x$ cannot be negative. So, $x=3$. $\therefore$ In $\triangle \mathrm{ADE}, \cos \alpha=\frac{\mathrm{x}}{6}=\frac{3}{6}=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \alpha=\frac{\pi}{3}$.

questions.q: What is the area of the region bounded by the parabolas $y^2=6(x-1)$ and $y^2=3 x ?$

$\begin{aligned} & y^2=6(x-1) \\ & \Rightarrow 6 x-6=y^2 \\ & \Rightarrow x=\frac{y^2+6}{6}=\frac{y^2}{6}+1 \end{aligned}$ Also, $\mathrm{y}^2=3 \mathrm{x} \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=\frac{\mathrm{y}^2}{3}$. Solving (1), (2), $3 \mathrm{x}=6(\mathrm{x}-1)\Rightarrow 3 \mathrm{x}=6 \mathrm{x}-6\Rightarrow 3 \mathrm{x}=6 \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=2$. $y^2=6 \Rightarrow y= \pm \sqrt{6}$. $\therefore \quad$ Area $\begin{aligned} & =\int_{-\sqrt{6}}^{\sqrt{6}}\left(\frac{y^2}{6}+1-\frac{y^2}{3}\right) \cdot d y=2 \int_0^{\sqrt{6}}\left(1-\frac{y^2}{6}\right) d y=2\left[y-\frac{y^3}{18}\right]_0^{\sqrt{6}} \\ & =2\left[\sqrt{6}-\frac{(\sqrt{6})^3}{18}\right]=2 \times \frac{2 \sqrt{6}}{3}=\frac{4 \sqrt{6}}{3} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: The equation $|1-x|+x^2=5$ has
options: a rational root and an irrational root
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& |1-x|+x^2=5 \\
& \Rightarrow|x-1|+x^2=5
\end{aligned}$
First case: If $x \lt 1,|x-1|$ is negative.
$\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \quad-(\mathrm{x}-1)+\mathrm{x}^2=5 \\
& \Rightarrow-\mathrm{x}+1+\mathrm{x}^2=5 \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}^2-\mathrm{x}+1=5 \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}^2-\mathrm{x}-4=0 \\
& \text { Roots are } \frac{-(-1) \pm \sqrt{(-1)^2-4(1)(-4)}}{2(1)}
\end{aligned}=\frac{1 \pm \sqrt{1+16}}{2}=\frac{1 \pm \sqrt{17}}{2}$
Since, $x \lt 1$, root cannot be $\frac{1+\sqrt{17}}{2}$. So, the root is $\frac{1-\sqrt{17}}{2}$, which is irrational.
Second case: If $x \gt 1,|x-1|=x-1\begin{array}{ll}
\therefore & |\mathrm{x}-1|+\mathrm{x}^2=5 \\
\Rightarrow & \mathrm{x}-1+\mathrm{x}^2=5 \\
\Rightarrow & \mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}-6=0 \\
\Rightarrow & \mathrm{x}^2+3 \mathrm{x}-2 \mathrm{x}-6=0 \\
\Rightarrow & \mathrm{x}(\mathrm{x}+3)-2(\mathrm{x}+3)=0 \\
\Rightarrow & \mathrm{x}=2,-3
\end{array}$
Since $x \gt 1$, root cannot be -3 . So, root is 2 which is rational.
$\therefore \quad$ given expression has one irrational root and one rational root.

questions.q: A sphere of constant radius $r$ through the origin intersects the coordinate axes in $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}$ and C . What is the locus of the centroid of the triangle ABC ?

(Squaring on both sides)
Let $(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)$ be centroid of sphere.
$\begin{aligned}
& \therefore(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)=\left(\frac{\mathrm{a}+0+0}{3}, \frac{0+\mathrm{b}+0}{3}, \frac{0+0+\mathrm{c}}{3}\right) \\
& =\left(\frac{\mathrm{a}}{3}, \frac{\mathrm{~b}}{3}, \frac{\mathrm{c}}{3}\right) \\

& =\frac{\mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{b}^2+\mathrm{c}^2}{9} \\
& =\frac{4 \mathrm{r}^2}{9}....from(1) \\
& \Rightarrow 9\left(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2\right)=4 \mathrm{r}^2
\end{aligned}$
So, Locus is $9\left(x^2+y^2+z^2\right)=4 r^2$.

questions.q: What is $\sin 105^{\circ}+\cos 105^{\circ}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \operatorname{Sin} 105^{\circ}+\cos 105^{\circ} \\ & =\sin \left(60^{\circ}+45^{\circ}\right)+\cos \left(60^{\circ}+45^{\circ}\right) \\ & =\left(\sin 60^{\circ} \cdot \cos 45^{\circ}+\cos 60^{\circ} \sin 45^{\circ}\right)+\left(\cos 60^{\circ} \cos 45^{\circ}\right. \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ & =\frac{2}{2 \sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: What is $\frac{\sin 5 x-\sin 3 x}{\cos 5 x+\cos 3 x}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\sin 5 x-\sin 3 x}{\cos 5 x+\cos 3 x} \\ & \sin c-\sin d=2 \cos \left(\frac{c+d}{2}\right) \sin \left(\frac{c-d}{2}\right) \\ & \cos c-\cos d=2 \cos \left(\frac{c+d}{2}\right) \cos \left(\frac{c-d}{2}\right) \\ & \therefore \frac{\sin 5 x-\sin 3 x}{\cos 5 x+\cos 3 x}=\frac{2 \cos \left(\frac{5 x+3 x}{2}\right) \sin \left(\frac{5 x-3 x}{2}\right)}{2 \cos \left(\frac{5 x+3 x}{2}\right) \cos \left(\frac{5 x-3 x}{2}\right)} \\ & =\frac{\sin \left(\frac{2 x}{2}\right)}{\cos \left(\frac{2 x}{2}\right)}=\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}=\tan x\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\frac{\sin (x+y)}{\sin (x-y)}=\frac{a+b}{a-b}$, then what is $\frac{\tan x}{\tan y}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\frac{\sin (x+y)}{\sin (x-y)}=\frac{a+b}{a-b}$
Applying componendo and dividendo, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\sin (x+y)+\sin (x-y)}{\sin (x+y)-\sin (x-y)}=\frac{a+b+a-b}{a+b-a+b} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{2 \sin \left(\frac{x+y+x-y}{2}\right) \cos \left(\frac{x+y-x+y}{2}\right)}{2 \cos \left(\frac{x+y+x-y}{2}\right) \sin \left(\frac{x+y-x+y}{2}\right)}=\frac{2 a}{2 b} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\sin x \cdot \cos y}{\cos x \cdot \sin y}=\frac{a}{b} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\tan x}{\tan y}=\frac{a}{b}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\sin \alpha+\sin \beta=0=\cos \alpha+\cos \beta$, where $0 \lt \beta \lt \alpha \lt 2 \pi$, then which one of the following is correct?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \sin \alpha+\sin \beta=0=\cos \alpha+\cos \beta \\ & \sin \alpha+\sin \beta=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \sin \alpha=-\sin \beta \\ & \Rightarrow \sin \alpha=\sin (\pi+\beta) \\ & \Rightarrow \alpha=\pi+\beta\end{aligned}$
